title: Latency seam scratchpad — arrival skew and dynamic model switch
content:
Purpose:
Quick informal log of arrival-skew experiments + a short exploration of dynamic model-switch penalty when switching to a quantized variant on overloaded hosts. This is a personal scratchpad — raw numbers, quick charts, open questions, and action items. Not polished.

Background / motivation:
- We see weird latency seams when incoming traffic distribution changes from uniform -> left-skewed (many small bursts) vs right-skewed (few heavy bursts stretched in time).
- Hypothesis: runtime scheduling + KV cache warming interacts with model-variant switching (fallbacks to q8/q4) and creates p99 spikes even when p50 looks stable.

Experiment setup (single-host locally instrumented):
- Model baseline: openmodel-v1.2 (float16) serving with local KV cache; fallback variant: openmodel-v1.2-q4 (quantized).
- HW: 1x A100-80GB emulation, host mem ample, single process runtime.
- Threading: 16 worker threads, async batching enabled, batch_max_tokens=4096, batch_timeout_ms=6.
- Arrival patterns tested:
  * uniform_poisson(lambda=200 qps)
  * left_skewed: 80% of requests in 20ms microbursts every 1s (avg 250 qps but high variance)
  * right_skewed: long tails, small frequent spikes but rarer heavy windows
  * bimodal: alternating low/high every 30s
- Payload sizes: mostly short prompts (avg 60 tokens), 20% long (avg 450 tokens) to exercise KV cache compaction.
- Duration: 12min per run, 2 warmup minutes excluded.

Key metrics collected:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 for end-to-end latency (ms)
- qps achieved and input arrival qps (to detect dropped/queued requests)
- batch size distribution (median, 95th percentile)
- model switch events: counts and time duration spent in fallback q4 variant
- KV cache hit-rate by token prefix

Representative raw results (trimmed):
1) uniform_poisson (avg arrival 200 qps)
- achieved qps: 198
- p50: 38ms, p90: 72ms, p95: 95ms, p99: 170ms
- median batch size: 8, batch p95: 18
- model-switch events: 0
- kv-hit-rate: 86%

2) left_skewed microbursts (25 microbursts/min)
- achieved qps: 210 (slight smoothing by batching)
- p50: 42ms, p90: 120ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 720ms (huge tails during bursts)
- median batch size: 6, batch p95: 32 (burst coalescing increases tail batches)
- model-switch events: 7 switches to q4 (avg penalty window 1.8s)
- kv-hit-rate: 72% (cache churn during bursts)

3) right_skewed long-tail windows
- achieved qps: 195
- p50: 40ms, p90: 78ms, p95: 110ms, p99: 260ms
- median batch size: 9, batch p95: 20
- model-switch events: 2 (short)
- kv-hit-rate: 81%

4) bimodal alternating 30s
- achieved qps: 203
- p50: 41ms, p90: 132ms, p95: 245ms, p99: 500ms
- model-switch events: 4 (coincident with high-window starts)
- kv-hit-rate: 69% on high windows

Observations / quick interpretation:
- The left_skewed microbursts produce catastrophic p99s despite average qps being similar or slightly higher than uniform. These tails line up with model-switch events and KV cache thrash.
- Model-switch events typically occur when concurrency crosses a threshold that triggers fallback policy (we artificially set fallback on sustained latency > X). But switches remain enabled long enough (avg 1.8s) for many requests to suffer degraded logits + longer overall scheduling overhead.
- Batch coalescing during microbursts increases batch size variance; large batches sometimes block small-reqs leading to queueing (head-of-line).
- KV cache hit-rate drop correlates with p95->p99 divergence.

Mini causal chain (suspected):
microburst -> sudden worker saturation -> runtime triggers fallback to quantized model (to keep throughput) -> new q4 model load/warm start + cache compaction -> increased tail latency while processes stabilize -> revert -> potential thrash if bursts continue.

Quick charts (ASCII, 12min run, aggregated windows):
- p99 trend (ms) by window: "25,28,30,35,40,110,320,45,30,28,60,720" (spike cluster around bursts)
- model switch count by minute: "0,0,0,1,0,2,0,0,0,1,0,3"

Notes on measurement fidelity / caveats:
- Single-host synthetic workload; real multi-tenant fleet will have additional noise.
- Fallback policy used here is slightly aggressive (intentionally) to provoke switches. Need to re-run with a more conservative hysteresis.
- We didn't instrument cold-start for q4 binary load time vs quantized inference warm-up separately; current model-switch duration includes both.
- Sampling for p99 may be sensitive to test harness clock skew; timestamps cross-checked with runtime traces (TRACE id list available in linked PR).

Experiments to run next (concrete):
1) Increase fallback hysteresis + add cooldown window of 10s. Expect fewer switches and lower p99. Quick run planned: 2025-02-19.
2) Separate the quantized variant load time: prefetch q4 binary in background when host sees rising queue depth (prefetch window). Measure additional mem overhead vs tail improvement.
3) Try a hybrid rolling fallback: prefer graceful degradation (reduce batch_max_tokens or increase batch_timeout) before switching model variant. Compare p99 and token-cost.
4) Add priority lanes: short prompts get a fastpath (dedicated worker pool) to avoid head-of-line blocking from large batch coalescence.
5) Re-run with multi-host topology (3 hosts) to include routing/fanout effects and cross-host cache miss patterns.

Quick wins to try this sprint:
- Adjust fallback policy constants (hysteresis + cooldown) in runtime config and run 1h smoke. Responsible: Diego.
- Add a lightweight q4 prefetch toggle behind flag to test binary pre-warming. Responsible: me (Rina) + Maya.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Where exactly does the biggest time cost happen during a switch? Binary load, JIT/compilation warmup, kernel selection, or KV cache rebuild? Need fine-grained traces.
- Is there a cheaper middle-ground than switching to q4 that preserves latency (e.g., temporarily reduce max_context or drop priority of long requests)?
- How much mem headroom do we need to keep q4 binaries resident on hot hosts? Tradeoffs vs cost.

Useful trace pointers and quick grep tokens (in runtime traces):
- TRACE token: "switch_to_quantized"
- timeline labels: "batch_coalesce_start", "kv_compact", "prefetch_q4_done"
- github perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412

Todo checklist (short):
- [ ] Add fine-grained timer around binary load path (Rina)
- [ ] Tweak fallback hysteresis + run smoke (Diego)
- [ ] Prototype q4 prefetch flag and measure mem/latency (Rina + Maya)
- [ ] Multi-host stress run next week (coordinate with SRE)

Notes to self: keep this one rough — aim to convert to a formal perf-brief if experiments show reproducible seam. If p99 reduces by >30% with hysteresis + prefetch, write up a one-pager for product + SRE.

End of scratchpad.
